column2: req_desc

Five reels on one hoarding.
The home page shows Now Showing, The Pack, The Lineup, Price Notices and End Credits in that order with the hero from Screens and layout, and under 768 wide its Reels navigation stays closed and unreachable until opened, then opens fully on screen and topmost at any point in the scroll without moving it, and stays correct through a pending read and a width crossing.

Exact seeded catalogue.
A first boot on an empty database holds exactly the Seed data records and nothing else, and a restart neither duplicates nor overwrites them.

Published counts from one reading.
The household buyer's first visit and the house editor's first sign-in both open on the seeded catalogue with the published counts line, both lines change together at the Kolkata midnight a scheduled revision takes effect, and the open editor's line updates in place after a publish.

Sticker Turn scrub.
Scrolling the pinned stage across four viewport heights publishes progress, yaw and camera distance that follow the Sticker Turn rules in both scroll directions.

Server-decided sticker.
The sticker seats only on a batch the server says carries one; on any other batch nothing lands and the mirror shows the no-sticker sentence.

Panel and mirror agree.
The pack panel and the DOM mirror state the same printed MRP, revised MRP, unit sale price, packed date and best-before date for the selected batch.

Sticker clear of the printed MRP.
For all four pack formats the published sticker rectangle never intersects the published printed MRP rectangle, so both prices stay readable.

Reduced-motion and no-WebGL stills.
With reduced motion the buyer picks Front, Back or Sticker stills with no scrub, and without WebGL an SVG panel carries the same facts, so no price fact is lost in either case.

Touch scrub.
On a touch phone an ordinary swipe scrolls the page natively and drives the same stage progress.

Lineup picks the pack.
Choosing a drink and pack in the lineup swaps the stage and mirror to that SKU's story batch and steps the neighbouring names down in brightness.

Pack reader.
Submitting a batch code shows that pack's facts from the one price decision, and only the latest read, lineup choice, search-result choice or history move ever reaches the stage, mirror, status and address, with no late answer or swap timer restoring anything older.

Published pack sentences.
Unknown-batch, no-sticker, past-date and unknown-pack situations show their published sentences character for character.

Batch lookup limit.
Batch lookups and batch-shaped pack searches beyond the published per-client limit answer 429 with Retry-After and a visible wait message, and the limit is exact under simultaneous requests.

Revision takes effect at Kolkata midnight.
A revision applies from 00:00 Asia/Kolkata on its effective date, decided by the server at read time with no restart or job, never from the client clock or browser zone, and identically in every process time zone.

Old packs and new packs.
A batch printed before a sticker revision's effective date shows its printed old MRP plus the sticker, and a batch printed on or after it shows the new MRP as print with no sticker, as qualified for new-print rows and old-wrapper batches in Business rules, and best-before edges fall at the published Kolkata instants.

Unit sale price and sugar.
Unit sale price and sugar per pack are derived by the published conversion and rounding rules, and unit sale price is omitted when it equals the retail price.

Release listings and current prices.
Price Notices lists every published notice as a release listing with old-to-revised prices and shows the current price of all SKUs, as tables at 768 and wider and stacked records below 768.

Printable notice PDF.
A notice version shows as Printable only after Gotenberg's PDF bytes are confirmed stored in MinIO, those stored bytes, an A4 document with the published fonts, title and fit, are what anyone downloads, and an open public notice page moves from pending to Printable in place with one announcement.

Printing outage and honest retry.
When a PDF cannot be rendered, the version shows Print failed, its download answers 503 with the published sentence, on-screen prices stay available, and the editor's retry keeps showing Print failed until the server accepts it.

Price sheet matching.
Each imported row, including Indian price formats, odd spacing and odd sizes, resolves by SKU code, remembered alias, or normalised name plus converted pack size, or lands as ambiguous or unmatched, with duplicates handled by the published rule and within the published import time.

Settling rows on the import desk.
The house editor settles ambiguous and unmatched rows on the import desk, and a settled description is remembered as one alias that also re-resolves open rows on every sheet and later imports, as qualified in Business rules.

Unsafe sheets refused.
A sheet that breaks a published upload rule is refused with its named reason and nothing is stored.

Re-import resolves to one sheet.
Importing the same file bytes again, even simultaneously, resolves to the same stored sheet, with its rows and settlements unchanged, one object and no second record.

Sheet evidence download.
The house editor can download any imported sheet byte for byte, including BOM and CRLF and under any stored file name, with its SHA-256 shown.

Notice drafted from a sheet by keyboard.
A sheet with no open rows drafts a notice that names the sheet's SHA-256 as its evidence and can be edited, and the whole path from file choice to saved draft works by keyboard with published focus moves worked out from the server's answer, while chosen unsettled values survive.

Sticker ceiling.
A sticker row above the published ceiling in integer paise blocks publish and is named, while new-print rows are not capped.

Publish transitions.
Notices move through the published state machine, every illegal transition is rejected with its exact status, and exactly one of several simultaneous publishes of one draft succeeds.

Signed notice messages.
Each published notice version produces one Svix-signed notice.published message with one stable event id per subscribed endpoint, verifiable with that endpoint's secret.

One price everywhere.
After a publish, the next load of the pack panel, mirror, pack reader, pack search results, current prices, notice, PDF, price sheet and message payload all state one price, and the publish preview reads the same decision.

Corrections keep history.
A correction creates a new version while the earlier version's wording and PDF stay downloadable and marked Superseded, naming the new version.

Correction reaches every channel.
Publishing a correction renders a new PDF, sends notice.corrected under a new event id, and changes the panel, mirror and sticker on the next load and the search result price on the next search.

Renames propagate with history.
A rename shows in place in the open editor and on the next load of the panel, lineup, current prices and price sheet, leaves each published notice under its published name, stays in the SKU's history with no gap under parallel renames, is treated as plain text everywhere, and never disturbs a later Drink or Pack choice.

Stockist price sheet.
A signed-in stockist downloads the current price sheet with the published columns, and any name or alias a spreadsheet could read as a command is made inert.

Endpoint address safety.
Saving or test-sending a message endpoint refuses unsafe addresses by the published rules, including embedded and reserved forms, checking on save and again before each test send, and simultaneous saves respect the limit and URL identity exactly.

Endpoint secrets and isolation.
An endpoint's signing secret is shown once, and a stockist sees only their own endpoints and delivery log.

Delivery log and redelivery.
The delivery log shows Delivered or Failed only from Svix attempts, lists those attempts, and lets the stockist request a redelivery of a failed message, whatever the server's clock says.

Messaging outage.
With Svix unreachable, publishes and endpoint saves still succeed, events stay pending, and the published queued sentence shows, as qualified in Services.

Sign-in and roles.
Seeded accounts sign in with email and password and land on their own screen, each role reaches only its own screens and endpoints, and an ended session sends the next action to sign-in with the published sentence.

Sign-in limit.
Failed sign-ins beyond the published per-client limit answer 429 with Retry-After and a visible wait message, and the limit is exact under simultaneous requests.

Published layouts.
Screens follow the published layouts at under 768, 768 to 1279, and 1280 and up, with no horizontal page scroll at 375, 768 or 1280 wide, and crossing a boundary with no reload keeps field text, open dialogs and focus.

Platform and server boundary.
The app runs from the run manifest, answers its health check, reads configuration from the environment, and enforces the published server boundary.

Marquee and motion discipline.
The price-change marquee runs current data and can be paused, published motion timings hold, and no unnamed decorative loop runs.

Keyboard and live regions.
Every control works by keyboard with visible focus and focus return, Tab stays inside an open dialog, and every async outcome is announced in its named live region.

Cinema hoarding look.
Every screen carries the published cinema hoarding direction, including the hero composition, the two typefaces, the field colours and the deliberately crooked sticker climax.

Credentials and real integrations.
Service credentials come only from the environment, delivery, print, search and stored-object states derive only from provider results, and panel facts come from the server price decision.

Old-wrapper run-out.
A sticker notice can set a run-out date, a batch registered as an old wrapper inside that window prints the old MRP plus its sticker on every surface, registrations or corrections outside the rule are refused with one winner when they race, and every limit counts Asia/Kolkata calendar days.

Rate continuity.
A sticker row whose old rate does not follow the SKU's last sticker rate is refused and named.

Revision order guard.
No publish or correction may add a row before, change or remove a row beneath, or move a date past another notice's later published row for that SKU.

Cross-draft races.
Simultaneous publishes of different drafts give exactly one winner per SKU and date and consecutive notice numbers, with no gap, no server error and no number spent on a refusal.

Draft lost update.
Saving or publishing a draft from a stale tab is refused with the published sentence, which stays through refreshes and preview answers until the next action in Publish status, and the typed values stay on screen.

Recovery without restart.
When Svix or Gotenberg returns with no restart, deferred and queued work completes exactly once as qualified in Services, and the queued sentence clears.

Endpoint lifecycle.
A stockist can rotate an endpoint's secret through Svix with both secrets verifying during the overlap and one winner among simultaneous rotations, and remove an endpoint, which frees its slot, keeps its log rows, cancels undelivered entries and stops delivery, with the row leaving the screen only on the server's answer.

Sticker Turn in pixels.
The stage publishes the on-screen printed MRP rectangle, sticker quad and panel rectangle every frame, and screenshots prove the published disjointness, colour, tilt, flight, zoom, foreshortening, grain, no-sticker and correction rules in both renderers and at the published device pixel ratios.

Scrub survives real use.
Reloading mid-scroll, resizing across a breakpoint, keyboard scrolling, a real touch swipe, a pack swap late in the scrub and Back from a notice page all keep the stage on its published formulas.

Lineup in the URL.
Choosing a lineup pack puts it in the address as a shareable link, Back and Forward restore the pack without moving the page, and batch and unknown links follow the published precedence.

Refreshes never disturb the user.
The 5-second refreshes keep field text, caret, focus, open dialogs and scroll, and each real print or delivery change is announced exactly once in its named live region.

One pack travels.
As the arch opens, the hero's pack moves continuously from the arch to the stage pack's position and size, reversibly and in both renderers, as published through its on-screen rectangle.

WebGL context loss.
When the stage loses its WebGL context it shows the SVG panel at the same progress and facts within one second, and on restoration it returns to WebGL within two seconds drawing the batch selected now.

Live publish preview.
Each draft and correction shows a live preview of old MRP, ceiling, the packs that take the sticker and the blocking refusal, updated from typed values without moving focus and without writing anything.

Preview equals publish.
For every publish check the preview's blocking error is deep-equal to the error the real publish or correction answers, and it spends no revision or number.

Recover failed messages.
A stockist can request redelivery of every failed entry with no outstanding request on one live endpoint, never resending anything else, also during an outage and under a skewed clock.

Providers that misbehave.
A provider that hangs, answers garbage, keeps refusing one event or loses an answer never hangs an action, stores a false PDF, holds up other events or creates a duplicate, as qualified in Services.

Typed work survives an ended session.
After a session ends, the same account's next sign-in in that tab restores typed draft, correction and endpoint values with the published sentence and sends nothing until the user acts, while another account or a deliberate sign-out discards them.

Work runs from an outbox.
Publish, correction, Retry print, test send, redelivery, recovery, rename and settled alias each write their work in the same Postgres transaction as their state change, and a relay carries it with confirmed publishes to the durable work queue in the published job bodies.

Workers survive a lost connection.
After a broker connection dies the server keeps running, consumers return within 15 seconds with no restart, and a render whose acknowledgement was lost leaves one stored PDF and one announcement.

Replays leave one effect.
Workers read current Postgres state and never data in the job body, so a replayed job cannot restore older search data, rewrite a PDF or create a second Svix message, and per endpoint a correction is never handed to Svix before the version it corrects is accepted.

Broken jobs set aside.
An unparseable job, an unknown kind or a missing target moves at once to the dead queue and raises the Held work count without delaying later work, a provider failure is never set aside however long the outage lasts, and each change reaches an open editor with focus and typed values unmoved, also behind a dialog.

Broker outage.
With RabbitMQ unreachable or hanging, health stays 200, all actions answer within 5 seconds, Publish notice now sends one request, versions stay Print pending while the next load of the public pack already states the new price, the published queued sentence shows, and within 30 seconds of its return all work completes once and the sentence clears.

Pack search.
A searchbox finds packs by drink name, SKU name, alias and notice title with published typo rules where every query word must match, while code-shaped queries are whole matches against Postgres with no typos.

Search reads the one price decision.
Result names, prices and source notices are read from Postgres when the search answers and the index holds no price, so a correction reaches result prices on the next search and a revision applies at Kolkata midnight with no job.

Search lag stated honestly.
A publish, correction, rename or settled alias reaches matching within 15 seconds, the search state stays behind until Meilisearch reports the task succeeded, and an earlier answer never replaces a later input's answer.

Search outage and rebuild.
With Meilisearch unreachable or hanging, search answers 200 within 5 seconds with its state down, code-shaped queries still answer, the no-match sentence never shows, and within 30 seconds of its return or of a wiped index the index matches Postgres with no restart.

Immutable stored objects.
Notice PDFs and original sheets live only in a private MinIO bucket under keys prefixed by the copy's id, are never rewritten or removed, answer 403 to an unsigned read, and an import during a storage fault leaves either an object with its sheet record or a named refusal with no sheet record, as qualified in Business rules.

Signed links renew in place.
Downloads go through 60-second signed links that an open page renews in place on a monotonic timer, keeping focus and scroll and announcing nothing, with an expired link removed and its sentence shown until a fresh one arrives.

Storage outage.
With MinIO unreachable or hanging, link and download requests answer 503 with the published sentence within 5 seconds, the sentence replaces the link in place, the print state stays printable, and the link returns within 30 seconds of its return with no reload.

Copies never collide.
Each copy of the app has its own random id in Postgres, and its queues, search index and object keys carry that id, so one copy's work, search hits and objects never reach another.

Every pack choice re-reads the server.
Every lineup, reader, search-result and Back or Forward choice re-reads the server and draws that answer with no client cache of facts, its swap running in the published time bands in both renderers, while everything else on an open public page stays as loaded except as qualified in Interactions.

Sticker flight and live stage changes.
The sticker's flight follows the published straight-line band, three context-loss and restore cycles keep one canvas and one context with the panel matching a fresh load, and changing the reduced-motion setting with no reload takes effect within 400 milliseconds in both directions.

Clear of the fixed layers.
On the home page at each published viewport, a control taking focus by keyboard, a jump or a result key is wholly on screen, clear of the fixed layers and topmost at its centre within 400 milliseconds, as qualified in Interactions, and the next wheel step continues from where it is.

Reels panel holds keyboard and tap.
Under 768 wide, while the Reels panel is open, Tab and Shift+Tab cycle only the Reels button and its five links, and a tap outside closes it, returns focus to Reels and activates nothing beneath.

New-day slip.
An open home page that finds the server's date has moved shows the New day slip without changing anything else, and Read today's prices re-reads the pack, marquee, listings, current prices and counts line in place, holding scroll and progress, as qualified in Interactions.

Turn slider.
A slider named Turn the pack inside the pinned view drives and follows the same progress by keyboard, thumb drag, wheel and swipe, also during a context loss, and is absent under reduced motion.

Pack front states the name.
Below yaw 90 every format draws the live drink name and variant inside the published front box in both renderers, the hero pack draws the same, an 80-character name leaves no ink outside the box, and both stage images carry the SKU name as their accessible description.

Confirm publish.
Publishing goes through a Confirm publish dialog that lists the packs that take the sticker, refuses to act on unsaved values, follows new blocking results while open, sends one request however often it is pressed, and leaves focus on the published target.

Refused rows lead to their fields.
When a preview or refusal names rows, a Refused rows list links each one to its Revised MRP field, which carries the error until the preview stops naming it.

Desk bar.
Under 1280 wide with any open row, the editor shows a sticky Desk bar with the server's open-row count and a Next open row button, and every desk focus move leaves the row's controls above the bar and topmost.

Result keys.
In Find a pack the arrow keys and Escape move between box and results as published, choosing keeps focus on the result, and a later answer replacing the list moves focus to the box.

Older versions collapse.
On a notice page the newest version is open and each older one is collapsed behind a Version button, with its closed body hidden from sight, the tab order and the accessibility tree, and the open state survives renewals, checks and width crossings.

Another account in this browser.
A stockist or editor tab that finds another account signed in, or gets a 403 forbidden, moves to that account's own screen on its next refresh with no sentence, discarding held values and showing nothing of the former account.

Wait timer.
On a 429 the wait message is announced once and a separate timer counts down each monotonic second, while Read pack or Sign in sends nothing and keeps typed values and focus, until at zero both clear silently.

Status survives a modal.
While any modal dialog is open, the page's outage alerts, its print or delivery status, its Held work line and its Work status stay in the accessibility tree exactly once and rise, update and clear on refreshes without moving focus or letting Tab leave the dialog.

A focused link goes and returns.
When a held link leaves while focused, focus moves to Print status and returns to the link if it comes back with focus still there, and a width crossing during a held mint leaves one link.

Long values and a pending removal.
Long URLs, hashes and event ids wrap with no horizontal page scroll at 375 wide with every row action reachable, the Signing secret dialog fits the viewport, and a pending removal survives refreshes and sends one DELETE.

Old wrapper stated on the pack.
The pack reader's facts name the notice that allows an old wrapper, so the mirror, panel and a link to that notice state it on every old-wrapper batch in both renderers.

Day read on a phone.
While Read today's prices is pending a further press sends nothing, a day check sent before the press is discarded whatever it answers, a newer pack choice cancels only the pack read while the rest of the day read completes, and at progress 0.75 or later the new sticker decision shows within 400 milliseconds of the pack answer.

Notice links on a phone.
Each version's download link renews on its own timer, also inside a closed body, a held mint for one version never removes another version's link, and at 375x812 a shown link is at least 44 pixels tall, topmost at its centre and opens that version's stored bytes on a tap.

Stockist row actions by touch.
While a Send test, Rotate secret, Recover failed or Redeliver request is unanswered that button keeps focus and a further press sends nothing, and at 375x812 every row action and delivery record action stays at least 44 pixels and topmost with a 2,048-character URL on the row, with focus kept on a Redeliver button across a 768 crossing.

Modals on a phone during an outage.
At each published viewport the three modal dialogs fit the viewport and scroll inside, an outage alert raised with one open is visible and clear of every dialog control, typed values, caret and focus survive it, and a pending correction sends one request and lands focus on the published target.

Honest print behind the Desk bar.
Under 1280 wide while the Desk bar shows, any control taking focus is wholly above the bar and topmost within 400 milliseconds, a pending Retry print sends nothing further while the version still reads Print failed, and a late Gotenberg answer stores and announces nothing.
/app/run.json exists with string install, build, serve and "_schema":"run-manifest-v1".
THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md at /app lists every shipped package, font and icon set with its licence; shipped packages means the production dependency tree (npm ls --omit=dev --all --json).

Every shipped package, meaning the production dependency tree (npm ls --omit=dev --all --json), has an MIT, Apache-2.0, BSD-2-Clause, BSD-3-Clause, ISC, 0BSD or CC0-1.0 licence, except a font package such as @fontsource/bebas-neue, which may be OFL-1.1; fonts are OFL-1.1.
Postgres is the system of record, MinIO holds bytes, Meilisearch holds a rebuildable index and RabbitMQ holds work, with no Redis, SQLite or product data written to local disk.
Bebas Neue, EB Garamond, Phosphor icons and the 3D code are shipped with the app and loaded from its own origin.
The repository contains no photo, raster pack image or 3D model file, because every pack is procedural.
The Seed data section ships exactly as printed, with no leftover development or test records.
The test clock is reachable only when INTERVAL_TEST_CLOCK is on, and no other test or debug endpoint ships.
